At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

At Genmab, we’re committed to building extra[not]ordinary futures together, by developing antibody products and pioneering, knock-your-socks-off therapies that change the lives of patients and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. From our people who are caring, candid, and impact-driven to our business, which is innovative and rooted in science, we believe that being proudly unique, determined to be our best, and authentic is essential to fulfilling our purpose.

The Role and Department

We are looking for an Associate Director, Technology Transfer Lead, to lead a team of Project Managers responsible for global process transfers in Genmab’s late-stage CMC organization. The scope covers biological intermediates (BI, e.g. monoclonal antibodies), chemical intermediates (CI), conjugated drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP).

You will report to the Senior Director, Head of Late-Stage Manufacturing Development Project Management, within Genmab Tech Ops in Denmark. You will work across CMC teams and technical functions, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Supply Chain to align transfers with program strategy and supply needs.

You will combine people leadership with oversight of transfers across sites and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs). You will lead selected complex transfers, ensuring receiving-site readiness, documented handover and continuity of supply.

**Responsibilities

****Team leadership and development

**

• Lead and develop a team of Project Managers, including resource planning, recruitment, performance management and professional development

• Coach team members in transfer leadership, stakeholder management and resolving issues across sites. Set clear expectations and encourage open dialogue and shared accountability

• Work with the Senior Director to align team priorities and resources with the transfer portfolio, address capacity constraints and strengthen collaboration across the project organization

**Global Process Transfer Responsibilities

**

• Translate transfer strategies into integrated plans with clear scope, ownership, milestones, budgets and dependencies across BI, CI, DS and DP

• Lead planning with sending and receiving sites, coordinating gap assessments, process and analytical knowledge transfer, and readiness of facilities, equipment, materials and documentation

• Coordinate engineering and GMP campaigns, comparability, process validation and regulatory activities with functional leads. Establish transfer acceptance criteria and ensure documented handover to routine manufacturing

• Maintain current plans and risk assessments, manage dependencies between transfer streams, and escalate issues with clear options and recommendations. Protect supply continuity throughout the transfer

CDMO collaboration and project governance

• Represent transfer programs in internal governance forums and relevant joint project and steering committees with CDMOs, within agreed responsibilities and decision authority

• Follow up on CDMO scope, deliverables, timelines and budgets with technical leads, Quality, External Manufacturing and Procurement. Prepare governance decisions and ensure agreed actions have clear owners and follow-up.

• Strengthen consistent transfer planning and readiness reviews, share lessons learned, and improve the Project Manual and tools. Support compliance with applicable quality processes in collaboration with Quality and functional experts

**Requirements

**

• 
Master’s degree or higher in natural sciences, pharmacy, engineering or a related discipline

• 
Extensive CMC experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including technology transfer and late-stage development or commercial manufacturing of biologics

• 
Demonstrated experience leading complex transfers between manufacturing sites and CDMOs, including integrated planning, budget management, risk management and coordination across regions

• 
Sound understanding of antibody manufacturing and the interfaces between BI, CI, conjugation and DP.

• 
Experience with antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) technology transfers is an advantage

• 
Practical understanding of process and analytical transfer, comparability, process validation, manufacturing readiness and the associated CMC submission requirements

• 
Working knowledge of GMP and global CMC regulatory expectations, and experience managing CDMO relationships and project governance.

• 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to explain complex issues, present recommendations and collaborate across functions and cultures.

**About You

**You enjoy developing people and taking responsibility for delivery. You set clear priorities, delegate effectively and remain available as a coach and sparring partner. You bring structure to complex transfers and act early when risks or competing demands arise.

You build constructive relationships with technical specialists and manufacturing partners, and challenge assumptions while maintaining trust. You connect decisions across the supply chain, exercise sound judgment and value a ONE-Team approach to delivering shared goals.

**Location and Travel

**The role is based in Denmark, with international travel to Genmab locations and external manufacturing partners.

Genmab leverages the effectiveness of an agile working environment, when possible, for the betterment of employee work-life balance. Our offices are designed as open, community-based spaces that work to connect our employees. Whether you’re in one of our collaboratively designed office spaces or working remotely, we thrive on connecting with each other to innovate.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK624.000,00---936.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

**About The Role

**At FLS, we have simplified our business and strengthened our profitability in recent years. We are now shifting our focus to accelerating profitable growth. To steer this journey, we are establishing a Corporate Growth Office that leads our strategic growth and profitability initiatives in close cooperation with our Business Lines, Group Functions and other stakeholders.

As Director, Corporate Growth Office and Strategy, you will build and run the engine that turns our strategic ambitions into owned, tracked and delivered results. You will own the portfolio management, governance and operating rhythm of the Corporate Growth Office. This spans the monthly Growth Office reviews in our Executive Leadership Team and in each Business Line performance review. You will also connect the initiative portfolio to our corporate strategy process. As deputy to the Head of Corporate Growth Office, you will be a trusted sparring partner to Business Line Presidents, Finance and initiative owners.

Reporting to the Head of Corporate Growth Office, you will join a small, high-calibre team at our headquarters in Copenhagen. Around 80% of the role is dedicated to running the Corporate Growth Office and around 20% to corporate strategy work. The Growth Office enables, challenges and connects: our Business Lines own the delivery of their initiatives, and you will make sure it happens with pace, rigour and transparency.

**What You Gain

**This is a rare opportunity to build a Growth Office from the ground up at a pivotal moment for FLS, and to shape how a global industrial company steers its growth. You will gain:

• Close collaboration with our CEO, the Executive Leadership Team and Business Line Presidents and Business Line management teams.

• An enterprise-wide view of how FLS creates value across Business Lines, Group Functions, sales areas and our mergers and acquisitions (M&A) agenda.

• Visible impact, as your work shows directly in our results and in how we work together as one FLS.

• A broad platform for your professional development, combining growth office leadership with corporate strategy.

• The chance to help the mining industry move towards a more sustainable future.

**You will play a key role in

**_Setting up and running the Corporate Growth Office

_

• Designing and embedding the Growth Office operating model with the Head of Corporate Growth Office, including governance forums, roles and decision rights, the stage-gate process, value rules and reporting standards.

• Turning our corporate management model into a working operating rhythm, including the monthly Growth Office review in the Executive Leadership Team and the Growth Office segment of each monthly Business Line performance review.

• Building an in-house playbook and capability, so that FLS eventually runs its growth agenda with its own people, tools and routines.

_Managing the growth portfolio

_

• Owning one Group-wide view of growth workstreams and initiatives, with clear owners, milestones, value targets, risks and interdependencies.

• Running the stage-gate process from idea to realised value, including gate-readiness checks and rigour tests before key decisions.

• Keeping the pipeline healthy through quarterly re-prioritisation and backfilling of initiatives, and spotting off-track initiatives early.

_Executive governance and reporting

_

• Preparing decision-ready material for the Executive Leadership Team and Business Line leadership on value delivered against plan, value at risk, stage-gate decisions and blockers.

• Maintaining decision and action logs, driving follow-up and escalating issues that need executive attention.

• Contributing to Executive Leadership Team and Board updates and to the messages cascaded to the wider organisation.

• Deputising for the Head of Corporate Growth Office in executive forums.

_Value tracking with Finance

_

• Defining the baselines, impact categories and validation rules that make reported value credible, together with Group and Business Line Finance.

• Reconciling initiative value with forecasts, budgets and actual results every month.

• Rolling out and governing a common initiative-tracking software platform as the single source of truth.

_Partnering with Business Lines and Group Functions

_

• Acting as the Growth Office’s lead partner for selected Business Lines and Functions and challenging the ambition, pace and quality of their plans.

• Helping each Business Line establish its own Growth Office cadence in line with our common practice.

• Coordinating cross-Business Line and cross-functional initiatives, and supporting the integration of acquisitions into the growth portfolio.

_Corporate strategy

_

• Supporting the annual strategy process and preparing strategy material for the Executive Leadership Team and the Board.

• Translating strategic and financial targets into Business Line growth ambitions, key performance indicators (KPIs) and initiative portfolios.

• Leading selected strategic analyses, such as market and competitor insights, growth levers and business cases.

_Building capability and a performance culture

_

• Training initiative owners and Business Line Growth Office leads in our ways of working, methods and tools.

• Working with Communications and People & Culture on the growth narrative, success stories and recognition.

• Promoting transparency, accountability and fact-based decision-making across the organisation.

**To succeed in the role, you

**_Experience and education

_

• Have at least eight years of professional experience, including several years with a leading management consultancy, or equivalent.

• Have hands-on experience of setting up and running a transformation, growth or program management office end to end, ideally in a growth or commercial transformation and not only in a cost program.

• Have led or steered large, cross-functional initiative portfolios with direct exposure to CEOs, executive teams and boards.

• Bring experience of strategy work, such as translating strategic targets into initiatives and KPIs; experience of running a corporate strategy process or M&A integration is an advantage.

• Ideally bring experience from industrial, capital goods, mining, energy or other business-to-business companies with a strong service business.

• Hold a master’s degree in business, economics, engineering or a related field; an MBA is an advantage.

_Knowledge and skills

_

• Know the mechanics of a well-run growth office: stage gates, value tracking and validation, governance cadence, performance dialogues and tracking tools.

• Have strong financial acumen, including profit and loss logic, business cases, baselines and impact validation, and work naturally with Finance.

• Understand commercial growth levers such as pricing, sales effectiveness, aftermarket and service growth, and product and portfolio management.

• Create clear, concise and decision-ready material and storylines in PowerPoint and Excel; experience with strategic program management tools is an advantage.

• Are fluent in English; other languages are an advantage.

_Personal qualities

_

• Have the executive presence and credibility to challenge senior leaders constructively and to influence without formal authority.

• Are highly structured, rigorous and detail-oriented, while staying pragmatic and focused on what moves the needle.

• Stay resilient and composed under pressure and in ambiguity.

• Are collaborative and inclusive, with a coaching mindset and a ‘one FLS’ attitude.

• Act with integrity and discretion when handling sensitive information.

• Are based in, or willing to relocate to, Copenhagen, and are able to travel when needed.

• Have a genuine interest in FLS, our customers, the mining industry and our MissionZero ambition.

Total salary range incl. variable pay: DKK 1,220,000–1,800,000 per year.

• The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

For more information about the role, please contact Anssi Poutanen, Head of Corporate Growth Office, at Anssi.Poutanen@FLSmidth.com. We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

As an equal opportunity employer, FLSmidth embraces diversity and equality by promoting an environment of inclusion. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds and perspectives to apply - the more diverse our employees are, the stronger our team is. In our commitment to equal opportunity and eliminating bias, we kindly request that you exclude personal information such as age, ethnicity, marital status, number of children, and photographs from your application materials.

FLSmidth is a full flowsheet technology and service supplier to the global mining industry. We enable our customers to improve performance, lower operating costs and reduce environmental impact. MissionZero is our sustainability ambition towards zero emissions in mining by 2030. We work within fully validated Science-Based Targets, have a clear commitment to improving the sustainability performance of the global mining industry and aim to become carbon neutral in our own operations by 2030. – for more information please visit FLSmidth.com/careers

We offer all employees access to a dedicated recognition platform, empowering you to celebrate achievements, share appreciation and stay connected globally.

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Project Engineer works hands-on with manufacturing and cross-functional teams to implement product and process changes for medical devices used in ultrasound, surgical visualization, and image-guided procedures.

The role supports manufacturing across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration and loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

This is a hands-on manufacturing engineering role, working directly with operators, technicians, engineers, and SMEs on the production floor to troubleshoot issues, execute trials and first builds, collect and evaluate data, implement process changes, and verify solutions in the actual manufacturing environment

The position combines practical manufacturing engineering with three core areas: ECO/NPI implementation and manufacturing readiness; NC, INV and CAPA activities and Equipment Qualification/Process Validation.

**Job Description

****This is an onsite opportunity at our manufacturing site in Herlev, Denmark.

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Lead ECO implementation, NPI, and manufacturing change activities from production impact assessment and cut-in strategy through implementation and closure.

• Coordinate first builds and production trials, including process updates, SOP/WI changes, training, data and evidence collection, and implementation reporting.

• Work hands-on with operators and technicians on the production floor to troubleshoot manufacturing issues, implement process changes, and verify solutions.

• Own and drive NC, INV, and CAPA activities (TrackWise), including investigations, root cause analysis, corrective actions, implementation, effectiveness checks, and closure.

• Facilitate root cause investigations and define corrective actions together with Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, and relevant SMEs.

• Lead and support Equipment Qualification and Process Validation, including risk assessments, validation planning, protocol execution, documentation, and reporting.

• Support URS, IQ/OQ/PQ, equipment qualification, test method validation, revalidation, and ongoing process review, as applicable.

• Develop and improve manufacturing processes using pFMEA, Control Plans, risk management, process controls, and continuous improvement.

• Ensure manufacturing changes, investigations, equipment, and processes are appropriately documented, controlled, validated, traceable, and audit-ready.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with manufacturing engineering, ECO implementation, NPI, or sustaining engineering.

• Experience with NC, INV, CAPA, root cause analysis, and Quality System workflows.

• Experience with or strong understanding of Equipment Qualification and Process Validation.

• Knowledge of GMP, Quality Management Systems, risk management, and manufacturing process controls.

• Experience working in medical device or other regulated manufacturing environments.

• Proven ability to work cross-functionally across Engineering, Manufacturing, and Quality.

**Desired Characteristics (nice to have)

**

• Hands-on experience with medical device manufacturing and manufacturing process development/improvement.

• Strong project execution and manufacturing change implementation skills.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root cause investigation capabilities.

• Experience with equipment qualification, process validation, and risk-based manufacturing activities.

• Structured and disciplined approach to documentation, workflows, actions, and deadlines.

• Proactive and solution-oriented with strong ownership and accountability.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.

• Ability to balance ECO/NPI, Quality System activities, validation, compliance, and production priorities

******Additional Information

******Relocation Assistance Provided: No

You’ll work with both SYBO platform services and third-party SDKs, participate in technical discussions around implementation, system design, and architecture, and become increasingly comfortable working across the Subway Surfers technology stack.

In your first twelve months, you’ll be a trusted and impactful member of the Subway Surfers team, contributing to technical systems and integrations from planning through release. You’ll help shape solutions across the game, platform integrations, and development pipeline that allow us to reliably deliver Subway Surfers to hundreds of millions of players.

• Good understanding of software engineering principles, data structures, algorithms, and common design patterns

Bonus points

If you join us, you'll have the opportunity to dive into exciting and creative projects alongside a diverse group of like-minded colleagues from over 40 countries across the globe.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious postdoc researcher for a 20-months position commencing 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management invites applicants for a postdoc position, dealing with the impact of sea-level rise and coastal squeeze on tidal flat evolution and sediment characteristics in coastal wetlands. The project is part of the research project ‘WadProof - Future-proofing the intertidal resource capital of the Danish Wadden Sea World Heritage Site’, funded by the Aage V. Jensen Charity Foundation.

  The research project

  The postdoc is part of the multidisciplinary ‘WadProof’ project focusing on advancing knowledge on the effects of sea-level rise and coastal squeeze on coastal wetland tidal flats sediment characteristics, the benthic fauna and the feeding opportunities for migratory birds in the Wadden Sea. The primary focus of the research will be to explore recent and historical changes in tidal flat development and texture, assess the effects of dikes and evaluate controlling drivers and forcing of tidal flat sediment characteristics and dynamics.

  The applicant will be collecting and analysing tidal flat surface sediment and core data, collect hydro- and sediment dynamic data and test remote sensing techniques using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and orthophoto to map intertidal marine sediment type distributions. During the fellowship there will be periods with fieldwork in the Wadden Sea, laboratory and course work, teaching and dissemination.

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of physical geography, marine geology or other geosciences. Applicants should have a PhD degree and interest in estuarine and coastal geomorphology and good communication skills in spoken and written English. Experience with collection and analysis of empirical data, including processing of satellite and UAV data is considered an advantage.

  Our group and research - and what do we offer?

  The postdoctoral  researcher will be a member of the research group ‘Geomorphology, processes and landscapes’ in the Section for Geography. The research group studies processes that shape coastal, estuarine, marine, fluvial and glacial landscapes. We work at multiple temporal and spatial scales ranging from grains to landscapes and from seconds to millennial. The group uses quantitative methods with a strong focus on empirical data collection to map, analyse and understand the physical processes that shape the earth surface. Our group currently comprises two professors, two associate professors, postdocs and PhD students.

  The group is a part of Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen. In the project you will be collaborating with researchers from Aarhus University and from the coastal department of the Danish Environmental Agency

  The postdoc’s duties will include research as well as teaching. The post may also include performance of other duties.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://ign.ku.dk/english/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Mikkel Fruergaard at email: mif@ign.ku.dk

  The position is open from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter, including the candidate’s motivation and a brief outline of suggested research contribution to the project (max 1,000 words). 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a complete publication list, conference presentation list, and overview of teaching experience. 	
• Documentation: Diplomas for Master’s and PhD degrees. If the PhD is not yet awarded, please specify the expected date of submission and/or defence in the CV. 	
• Publications: Up to five selected articles (published or unpublished). The selected articles must be uploaded as attachments and marked with an asterisk (*) on the publication list.   The deadline for applications is 29 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews will be held during week 1 in 2027.

Job Description

At Traitomic, we help companies unlock the potential of biology to create better-performing crops and microbes. Across agriculture, food and biotech, companies need biological solutions that deliver higher impact and reach the market faster. Whether starting from a genetic target, a desired phenotype or a commercial objective, Traitomic bridges the gap between biological potential and market-ready traits. Combining gene discovery, a proprietary non-GM/non-GE trait development process and deep scientific expertise, we accelerate the development of tailored crop and microbial improvements with unprecedented speed and specificity.

As part of our next phase of growth and long-term goals, we are expanding our in-house Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) and Data analysis platform in Copenhagen to support our Trait Development projects across microbial, plant, fungi and algae projects. jobs.description:
Location: _Søborg, Denmark. Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

_Are you the type of person who enjoys understanding how things work, questioning assumptions, and solving complex technical problems?

We are looking for a Sr Reliability Engineer to help shape the future of our maintenance, calibration and asset management programs. This is not a traditional maintenance role. Instead, you will focus on understanding equipment risks, analysing failure mechanisms, evaluating maintenance effectiveness, and developing data-driven maintenance and calibration strategies.

Some days you will be deep in equipment data, conducting component-level risk assessments and reliability analyses. Other days you will be presenting your recommendations, challenging established practices, and facilitating discussions with stakeholders across Manufacturing, Quality, Compliance, Engineering, and Maintenance.

Whether you are an experienced reliability professional or an exceptional early-career engineer with strong analytical abilities, we are interested in hearing from you.

**What You'll Be Doing

**Risk Assessment & Reliability Engineering

• Perform detailed equipment, instrument and component-level risk assessments.

• Identify failure modes and evaluate their impact on safety, compliance, reliability, and operational performance.

• Conduct FMECA, criticality assessments, root cause analyses, and other reliability studies.

• Support a risk-based approach to maintenance decision-making.

Maintenance & Calibration Strategy Development

• Evaluate existing maintenance and calibration programs and challenge activities that do not deliver value.

• Redesign and optimize preventive, predictive, corrective, and condition-based maintenance and calibration strategies.

• Build maintenance and calibration programs based on risk, data, and equipment criticality.

• Develop practical recommendations that improve equipment reliability while optimizing resource utilization.

Data Analysis & Continuous Improvement

• Analyse maintenance and calibration history, failure data, asset performance trends, and reliability metrics.

• Identify patterns, recurring issues, and improvement opportunities.

• Convert complex data into actionable recommendations.

• Support the development of KPIs and performance monitoring tools.

• Support digitalization initiatives that improve data visibility, decision-making, and maintenance effectiveness across the organization.

• Develop and maintain reporting and analytical tools, including Power BI dashboards and visualizations, to support reliability, risk, and maintenance strategy decisions.

Stakeholder Collaboration

• Work closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Compliance, Engineering, and Maintenance teams.

• Facilitate discussions where priorities may differ and help build alignment around technical decisions.

• Present findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Support internal and external audits by presenting maintenance strategies, risk assessments, and technical rationales, and by clearly communicating decisions to auditors and regulatory stakeholders.

• Act as a subject matter expert during audits and inspections, presenting risk assessments, maintenance strategies, and technical justifications to auditors, Quality, and Compliance stakeholders.

**What We're Looking For

**We are less interested in the number of years on your CV and more interested in how you think.

**You Are Likely Someone Who

**

• Enjoys analysing complex technical problems.

• Is naturally curious and asks "why" before accepting a conclusion.

• Can work independently and stay focused on difficult problems.

• Is comfortable challenging established ways of working when supported by facts and data.

• Can communicate confidently with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

• Is persistent, resilient, and comfortable navigating disagreement.

• Can balance technical rigor with practical business realities.

**Qualifications

**You may be an experienced engineer or a recent graduate.

**We'd Like To See

**

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related technical discipline.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

• Interest in asset reliability, maintenance optimization, risk management, or data analysis.

• Ability to work with complex datasets and draw meaningful conclusions.

• Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, P&IDs, User Requirement Specifications, Technical Specifications, and equipment manufacturer manuals.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Fluency in English.

Experience with the following is considered an advantage but is not required:

• FMECA

• FMEA

• RCM (Reliability Centred Maintenance)

• Root Cause Analysis

• Asset Criticality Assessments

• Reliability Engineering

• Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS)

• Manufacturing, pharmaceutical, biotech, food, chemical, or process industries

Who Will Thrive in This Role?

**This Role Is Likely a Great Fit If You

**

• Enjoy working independently and becoming an expert in a technical area.

• Like digging into data until you fully understand a problem.

• Are comfortable having difficult conversations when the facts support your position.

• Prefer solving root causes rather than treating symptoms.

• Enjoy building new solutions instead of simply maintaining existing processes.

• Enjoy understanding how equipment works by combining field observations with technical drawings, P&IDs, manuals, performance data, and engineering principles.

• Want to have a genuine impact on how maintenance and reliability decisions are made.

What We Offer

• A unique opportunity to shape and improve maintenance strategy across critical assets.

• Exposure to cross-functional decision-making and collaboration with senior stakeholders.

• Significant autonomy, ownership, and freedom to drive improvements.

• An environment that values analytical thinking, curiosity, and continuous improvement.

• Opportunities for professional growth regardless of your level of experience.

• A highly visible role with the opportunity to influence decisions, drive change, and provide informal leadership across the organization.

**Join our team

**We are eager to welcome a new colleague as soon as possible. Please submit your application no later than 30 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found.

Please apply exclusively through our recruitment system. Applications submitted through other channels will not be considered.

To support an inclusive and unbiased recruitment process, please do not include a photo in your CV. At AGC Biologics, we are committed to fair hiring practices and value diversity and inclusion throughout our recruitment process.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Sameer Ahmed, Senior Manager, Equipment Maintenance, at **sameer.ahmed@agc.com

**Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

We look forward to receiving your application!

**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

About TDC Brands

TDC Brands is home to YouSee, TDC Erhverv, Telmore, Hiper, eesy and Relatel — around 3,000 employees and roughly 6 million consumer and business customer relationships in Denmark. We are the commercial and service side of Danish telecom; TDC NET owns and runs the physical network.

We are putting AI to work across customer service, digital channels, sales and our own internal operations. Doing that in a company millions of Danes rely on means doing it carefully.

Why this role exists

AI governance fails in one of two ways. It becomes a review gate that slows everything down, or it becomes a document nobody reads. We want neither.

This role keeps governance close to the work. You’ll own the practical machinery — the use-case inventory, the risk assessments, the evaluation and testing — and you’ll sit inside the proof-of-concepts as they are built, not review them afterwards. It is a rare combination of skills, and a good place to build a career: governance people who can actually build are scarce, and getting scarcer.

What you’ll do

• Own the agent inventory. Maintain a live picture of every AI agent we run, and of the copilots, RAG applications and embedded model features around them — what each one does, what data and systems it can reach, what it is allowed to do without a human, who owns it, and where it sits against EU AI Act risk categories.

• Run the assessments. Work through risk, privacy and security reviews with Legal, Privacy and Security colleagues, and turn their requirements into something an engineering team can act on.

• Test what we build. Design and run evaluations: accuracy, hallucination, bias, prompt injection, tool misuse and failure behaviour. Build the test sets and keep them current as models and agents change.

• Help build the proof-of-concepts. Work hands-on alongside the AI Evangelist and delivery teams — preparing data, writing and refining prompts, wiring up APIs, measuring whether the thing actually works.

• Document it properly. Model cards, decision records and system documentation that stand up to an audit and are still readable by the people who have to use them.

• Watch the horizon. Track regulation, guidance and tooling as they evolve, and translate them into short, practical checklists rather than long policy documents.

Your first year

• A complete, trusted inventory across the six brands — agents and the AI applications around them — with risk classifications and ownership everyone agrees on.

• A working evaluation approach applied to at least two production or near-production systems.

• Assessment and documentation templates that teams reach for because they save time, not because they are mandatory.

• A reputation as the person engineers invite into a project early rather than call at the end.

What we’re looking for

• Around 4 years’ experience in data, AI, technology risk, compliance or a closely related field.

• Enough hands-on ability to be useful in a prototype: Python at a practical level — notebooks, scripts, calling APIs — and comfort with how LLM applications are put together. You do not need to be a software engineer.

• A working understanding of GDPR, and genuine interest in the EU AI Act and what it means in practice.

• Clear, structured writing. Much of this job is making complicated things legible to someone who has fifteen minutes.

• The confidence to ask an uncomfortable question in a room of senior people, and the judgement to know which questions are worth asking.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, we’d still like to hear from you.

Also useful, not required

• Experience in a regulated industry — telecom, finance, health or public sector.

• Familiarity with evaluation tooling and frameworks for LLM applications.

• Experience with Azure AI, AWS or Google Cloud AI services.

• Exposure to ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF or similar management frameworks.

• Danish language skills — useful for stakeholder work, but not a requirement.

What you’ll get out of it

• Direct mentoring from senior AI and architecture colleagues, and close work with Legal, Privacy and Security.

• Visibility across six brands and both consumer and business markets — unusual breadth for an early-career role.

• A seat at the table while an enterprise AI practice is being built, rather than inheriting one already built.

Practical details

• Team: You’ll join Data & AI, a team of around 40 people, working alongside the Senior AI Evangelist.

• Language: English is our main language of communication. Danish is an advantage.

If you care about doing full-stack development the right way – through clean architecture, automation, CI/CD, IaC, observability, golden paths, and engineering foundations – you’ll feel right at home at the Tech Collective, where we combine deep technical skills with real client impact.

**What You’ll Do

**Life as a consultant is different from a typical in-house role. At the Tech Collective, consulting means working on a wide range of projects with various clients – so you'll regularly encounter new challenges and have plenty of opportunities to grow your skills quickly.

We believe AI and agentic coding accelerate great developer practices – they do not replace them. That’s why solid architecture, quality, security, maintainability, and sound technical judgement matter more than ever.

In this senior role, you’ll help us understand client needs and turn them into real outcomes by taking technical ownership, guiding teams, and delivering robust solutions from idea to production.

• Build, test, and deliver software using modern engineering practices such as everything-as-code, CI/CD, GitOps, automation, and open-source principles

• Act as a trusted advisor to clients, helping them make great decisions and turn ideas into practical solutions

• Work across frontend and backend technologies, taking part in architectural decisions, system design, containerised environments, and clear, maintainable documentation

• Improve developer and user experience by shifting quality left, applying strong design principles, mentoring others, and delivering minimum viable products with a clear path to scale

• Design, build, and operate platforms and infrastructure, including APIs, CLIs, platform engineering, immutable infrastructure, and internal developer platforms

• Collaborate, teach, and lead through effective communication, technical writing, code reviews, lean principles, and strong data and security practices

• Lead technical workstreams and collaborate closely with clients, translating business needs into pragmatic technical solutions

**What You’ll Bring

**One thing that can be said of all your future colleagues is that we’re curious by nature, have a team-first mindset, a good sense of humour, and clear opinions on how tech can create value for our clients. If this sounds like you, you’ll be a great fit at The Tech Collective.

We’re looking for people with a relevant M.Sc. (this is mandatory and could be, for example, in computer science or software engineering) who are based within commuting distance of our office in Copenhagen.

**We’re looking for someone with a minimum of 5 years of professional experience in full-stack software development or similar engineering roles.

**On top of that, the ideal candidate is someone who brings senior engineering experience and:

• Communicates clearly in both written and spoken English

• Shares our values around software quality and delivery

• Enjoys working closely with clients and building trusted relationships with them

• Is tool-agnostic and chooses the right tool for the job

• Is comfortable with complexity and able to break problems down into manageable pieces

• Has solid experience building and operating modern software systems in production

• Understands software architecture, system design, testing, security, and maintainability

• Can guide technical decisions, challenge assumptions, and communicate trade-offs clearly

• Has experience mentoring or supporting other developers through code reviews, pairing, or technical sparring

Please note that you don’t need to meet all the criteria. The most important thing is that you have an engineering foundation, a senior mindset, consulting skills and curiosity to keep learning and growing.

**What We Offer

**When you step into our office, you step into a world of nerdery – and we love it and intend to keep it that way. You’ll become part of a low-ego, high-trust team of sharp engineers who you’ll work closely with from day one.

**Working With Us Means

**

• Real autonomy, real impact: you’ll own features end to end and lean into the tech you care most about.

• Growth that matters: a learning programme, mentoring, and plenty of peer knowledge sharing.

• Community and craft: strategy trips, meetups, and events across The Tech Collective/Implement Consulting Group.

At Eriksholm Research Centre, we are looking for a technically strong and practically minded Senior Research DSP Engineer to join our scientific team. You will help mature promising research ideas into robust concepts, demonstrators, and technical solutions that can move closer to adoption by R&D.

About the position

Eriksholm generates scientific insights and explores new technologies with the potential to improve future hearing care. We work closely with scientists, engineers, and Oticon R&D to ensure that promising ideas can be translated into solutions with meaningful impact for people with hearing loss.

In this position, you will bridge scientific exploration and engineering implementation. You will combine strong digital signal processing and acoustics expertise with hands-on experimental work, modelling, and prototype development.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Designing acoustic measurements and experimental laboratory setups.

• Building models and tools for analysing and validating technical concepts.

• Supporting the maturation and technical transfer of promising research solutions towards R&D.

The ideal candidate

You are curious, analytical, and motivated by solving complex technical problems. You enjoy moving between theory, modelling, implementation, and hands-on laboratory work. You are comfortable working with early-stage ideas where the path forward is not always fully defined.

You take ownership of your work, communicate technical topics clearly, and collaborate well with colleagues from different scientific and engineering disciplines. You also understand the importance of balancing scientific ambition with the practical requirements needed to bring a concept closer to product development.

We expect that you have:

• A master’s degree in electrical engineering, acoustical engineering, signal processing, or a related technical discipline.

• Several years of relevant experience in hearing-aid development, audio technology, or another technically related area. Experience from product development, research, technology exploration, or advanced engineering would all provide a strong foundation for this role.

• Strong knowledge of digital signal processing and acoustics.

• Experience with acoustic measurements, laboratory setups, modelling, and technical validation.

• Experience developing and evaluating algorithms in environments such as MATLAB, Python, or similar tools.

• The ability to translate complex technical challenges into structured experiments and practical solutions.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills.

• Professional proficiency in English.

Your workplace

The position is based on our site in Snekkersten, where you will work closely with Eriksholm’s multidisciplinary scientific community.

Eriksholm Research Centre is part of Oticon’s R&D organization. We pursue audiological discoveries with the potential to enhance customer and end-user benefits in future hearing care and work to ensure that scientific insights can be applied in solutions supporting people with hearing loss.

We are a multicultural and multidisciplinary team that values scientific integrity, collaboration, mutual respect, and openness. Our informal environment provides room to explore new ideas, challenge assumptions, and take considered technical risks.

Are you passionate about? Do you have experience within financial control and governance?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Head of Europe financial control and governance.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Head of Europe financial control and governance to join our growing team. As a key member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in Europe regional oversight, assurance and coordination across European entities. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will be joining the finance operations team consisting of 33 colleagues, and report directly to Cicek Wrabetz, Head of Europe Finance Operations who is based in Munich, Germany. You will be based in Hellerup, Denmark.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Lead regional governance and assurance. Maintain oversight of material accounting, reporting, control and compliance matters across Europe. Identify gaps, clarify ownership and coordinate resolution across teams and countries

• Oversee financial reporting and accounting. Coordinate statutory reporting and external audits across European jurisdictions and provide assurance over close, financial reporting and internal controls

• Navigate local requirements. Bring structure to country-specific requirements, including withholding tax, statutory obligations and invoicing, working closely with Tax, Legal, Compliance, Treasury and relevant process owners

• Drive launch and change readiness. Represent the European financial-control and governance perspective in new-market and entity launches, identifying local requirements and impacts across processes, systems, data and controls

• Simplify and strengthen ways of working. Challenge unnecessary complexity, country variations and manual workarounds. Identify root causes, clarify ownership and help implement compliant, scalable and sustainable solutions

• Leverage technology, AI and automation. Partner with Finance Systems and process owners to translate business needs and pain points into well-defined, controllable and scalable solutions, using technology where it creates meaningful value

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a MBA or Bachelor of Management /Economics/ business administration or equivalent - and 10+ years of experience including meaningful responsibility for accounting, financial operations, monthly close, managing external accountants, auditors and controls.

Furthermore, you have:

• 5+ years of experience within external or internal audit, controllership, financial control, Finance Operations, transformation, or a related field in an international environment

• Strong knowledge of accounting, IFRS, internal controls, audit, and European statutory and regulatory requirements

• A professional qualification such as CPA, Cand.merc.aud., ACCA, Wirtschaftsprüfer, or equivalent is preferred

• Demonstrated experience in strengthening controls, redesigning processes, and simplifying ways of working

• Experience working across countries and functions, including O2C, P2P, R2R, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Compliance, and Finance Systems

• Interest in and hands-on experience with ERP systems, analytics, automation, AI, or digital finance initiatives. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 is an advantage

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to

• Challenge complexity and has evidence of making processes simpler, stronger or more scalable

• Collaborate across functions and geographies and influences without relying on formal authority

• Balance control, compliance, business needs and practical implementation

Travel: 10-20 days per year.
